text:
Anya: Heads up — running into inconsistent behavior across SDKs when we attach per-request routing and quota metadata to traces. Should these be span attributes, baggage, or a resource attribute? Current: python wrapper adds both attr + baggage, go sets only attrs, rust leaves some keys out because OTLP exporter drops high-cardinality keys. Any strong opinions?
Mike: Don't use baggage for telemetry. Baggage is for propagation to downstream services/apps, not for storage/metrics. Use span attributes with stable keys, but keep them low-cardinality. If something is high-cardinality (user id, request id) drop or put in logs. :thinking:
Sophie: FWIW python OTLP exporter lets you set attribute limits and will truncate. Go's sdk has different defaults (no truncation until exporter), and rust's still pretty minimal. Example we could standardize on:
```python
# python wrapper pseudocode
span.set_attribute("redwood.routing.policy", "latency-pref")
span.set_attribute("redwood.quota.bucket", "tier-2")
# avoid: span.set_baggage_item("routing_policy", "latency-pref")
```
```go
// go wrapper pseudocode
span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("redwood.routing.policy", "latency-pref"))
```
Sophie: Also recommend normalizing keys to redwood.* so dashboards and retention rules can target them easily.
Kevin: Agree on normalization. On retention/exporter side we should configure the collector to do attribute processor trimming and keep a top-N for any dynamic attribute. That lets apps emit richer attrs and the pipeline drops noisy ones before long-term storage. Also consider sampling rules: keep 1% of traces with high-cardinality attrs for debugging.
Sam: Rust SDK note: there's no baked-in attr-limit config in our wrapper today. We could add a small sanitizer that drops keys matching a regex set or by a per-span count threshold before sending. That would bring parity.
Anya: Sounds good. Quick debate: should routing metadata ever be a resource attribute? I feel no — resource is static per service/host. Routing is per request so span attr is right.
Mike: +1. Resource for service-level metadata only. If you need propagation to downstream services, add a small, stable baggage key (but not high-cardinality).
Sophie: Actionable plan:
- Add attr whitelist + per-span attr limit to python/go/rust wrappers (normalize keys to redwood.*)
- Update opentelemetry-collector config: attribute processor + sampling rules to keep tail traces
- Update Console dashboards to query redwood.routing.* and redwood.quota.* keys and show count of dropped attrs metric
Anya: I'll draft a tiny RFC and list required config knobs. Who can take SDK PRs?
Kevin: I can take Go this week.
Sam: I'll do Rust, but will need an extra day for integration tests.
Sophie: I'll open the python PR today.
OTELBot: Deploy notice: opentelemetry-collector config PR #1234 merged to staging — attribute processor added. :rocket:
Mike: One more thing — emit a metric when we drop an attribute so ops can see attr churn and we can tune whitelist.
Anya: Good call. Add redwood.telemetry.attr_dropped_count with labels: sdk, key_pattern.
Sophie: PRs: python #567, link: https://git.redwood/py-wrapper/pull/567 :thumbsup:
Anya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll sync in tomorrow standup — I'll include the RFC link.
